endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: This authorization scope should be reviewed whenever the system's capabilities or integrations change.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether reviewing an agentic AI's access scope after capability or integration changes prevents access beyond what was authorized, and no study documents how often that hazard occurs. The recommendation currently rests on a single governance framework, the CHAI playbooks, which states that the scope should be reviewed.

perspectives.view: The supplied record contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty for the practice's effect is therefore rated as no direct evidence. The only support is one framework endorsement, which reflects expert judgment rather than measured outcomes.

The single endorsing source is the CHAI governance playbooks, which use "should" language. This is voluntary framework guidance. The supplied materials cite no statute, regulation, or agency requirement that mandates scope review when an agent's capabilities change.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that first measure how often agentic AI systems in health care acquire data or system access beyond their authorized scope after updates or new integrations. Those studies should then compare sites that conduct scope reviews at each change with sites that do not, reporting unauthorized-access events, time to detection, and staff time per review.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested this practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Whether scope review is feasible in lower-resourced systems, and whether access errors fall differently on these patients' records, remains unknown.
